extracted.intended_audience: Users of Mathematics Stack Exchange (askers and answerers) seeking guidance on when to use the 'definition' tag
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for posting and answering Math.SE questions that ask for, clarify, compare, or propose mathematical definitions. Covers what kinds of questions belong under the 'definition' tag and what scope is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting definitions of mathematical terms
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: "For requesting, clarifying, and comparing definitions of mathematical terms." Use this tag when the question's core is asking "What is X?" in a mathematical sense—i.e., asking for a definition or an explanation of a term or concept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarifying complicated definitions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: "Definitions are at the core of mathematical precision; they answer the question 'What is X?' in mathematics." Use the tag for questions that seek to make sense of or unpack a complex definition, explain parts of a definition, or resolve ambiguities in how a definition is stated or interpreted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparing/equivalence of definitions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: "Into this category fit questions regarding equivalence of definitions..." Use this tag when asking whether two (or more) given definitions define the same notion, or how they relate to one another (implications, equivalences, or differences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposing new definitions and seeking feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed new definitions for mathematical notions, with requests for improvements or comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: "...or proposed new definitions for mathematical notions, with requests for improvements or comments." Use this tag when the question contains a candidate definition and asks the community to critique, improve, or evaluate its suitability, precision, or consequences.
